**Paid Sick Leave Policy – California & New York** *Effective Date: [Insert date]* *Reviewed by: HR Department* --- ### 1. Purpose To provide all employees with paid sick leave that meets or exceeds the statutory requirements in both California and New York while keeping the policy simple, consistent across sites, and compliant with each state’s law. --- ### 2. Eligibility - All full‑time and part‑time employees who work **≥ 30 hours per year** are eligible for paid sick leave under this policy. - Employees in both states are covered regardless of job classification or location (California or New York). --- ### 3. Accrual Rate - **Accrual:** Employees accrue **1 hour of paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked**. - Accrual is calculated monthly based on the actual hours worked in the preceding month and added to the employee’s balance at the end of that month. --- ### 4. Maximum Accrual - The **maximum accrual cap is 40 hours per calendar year**. - *California:* Statutory maximum is 48 hours; capping at 40 hours remains within the allowed range. - *New York:* For businesses with < 100 employees (our company), the statutory maximum is 40 hours. - Once an employee reaches the cap, no additional sick leave will accrue until unused hours are taken. --- ### 5. Use of Sick Leave | State | Minimum Waiting Period | Usage Conditions | |-------|------------------------|------------------| | California | **90 days** after hire (unless employer allows earlier use) | May be used for:
• Employee’s own illness, injury or medical appointment
• Care of an immediate family member (spouse, child, parent, grandparent, sibling, domestic partner, etc.) | | New York | **No waiting period** – may begin using from the first day of employment | Same usage conditions as California | **Policy Provision:** Employees in both states may begin using accrued sick leave **from their first day of employment**. This is permissible under California law (the employer may allow earlier use) and satisfies New York’s requirement for immediate availability. - Sick leave can be taken in increments of at least 1 hour; the company will accept a minimum of 30 minutes if requested, provided it does not exceed the employee’s accrued balance. - Employees must provide notice to their supervisor as soon as practicable. For absences longer than one day, a medical certification may be required per state law. --- ### 6. Carry‑Over - Unused sick leave **carries over** to the next calendar year up to the maximum cap of 40 hours. - No additional carry‑over beyond the cap is permitted. --- ### 7. Interaction with Existing Paid Time Off (PTO) - This paid sick leave policy is **separate from the existing 10 days of PTO**. - Employees may choose to convert unused PTO into sick leave only if they elect to do so; conversion is not mandatory and does not affect statutory accruals. --- ### 8. Recordkeeping - The company will maintain accurate records of hours worked, accrued sick leave, usage, and balances for each employee in compliance with California’s “Accrual Tracking” requirements and New York’s “Record‑Keeping” provisions. - Employees can view their current balance through the HR portal or by requesting a statement from HR. --- ### 9. Enforcement & Misuse - Unlawful use of sick leave (e.g., using it for non‑qualifying reasons) may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination, consistent with company policy. - Employees who misuse sick leave will be required to repay the amount taken without pay. --- ### 10. Policy Review & Amendments - This policy will be reviewed annually or whenever state law changes. - Any amendments will be communicated in writing and posted on the intranet. --- **By signing below, I acknowledge that I have read, understand, and agree to comply with this Paid Sick Leave Policy.** Employee Signature: ________________________ Date: ___________ HR Representative: _________________________ Date: ___________ --- *This policy satisfies California’s Healthy Workplaces Act (minimum accrual of 1 hr/30 hrs worked; maximum 48 hrs) and New York’s Paid Sick Leave Law (minimum accrual of 1 hr/30 hrs worked; maximum 40 hrs for <100 employees). By capping at 40 hours, the company remains within both states’ statutory limits while providing a single, clear policy across all locations.*
